review_notes: The file is one theorem and has no simp attributes of its own. I read it in full, then read the definition of inclBaseChange in Def_CerednikDrinfeld_FormalUpperHalfPlaneDatum.lean. I searched for existing simp or API lemmas about inclBaseChange. The only evaluation lemma is inclBaseChange_tmul, which is proved by rfl and re-declared privately in several solution files. None of those copies is tagged simp, and the definitions file has no such lemma. I did not run Lean. I did not check whether adding the lemma as simp would conflict with other simp lemmas, such as the generic baseChange_tmul. Because inclBaseChange is a plain noncomputable def, the generic lemma would not fire on it unless the definition is unfolded.

findings.problem: The proof needs the evaluation rule for `inclBaseChange` on a pure tensor. That rule is not in the simp set or the API, so the proof proves it inline with `rfl` and then applies it with `rw [hincl] at hpush`. `inclBaseChange` is an irreducible-looking `def` (`(Submodule.inclusion h).baseChange B`), so `simp` cannot normalise `inclBaseChange B h (b ⊗ₜ v)` to `b ⊗ₜ ⟨v, h v.2⟩`. The same rule, `inclBaseChange_tmul`, is re-proved by `rfl` as a separate private theorem in at least three solution files. In each of them it is used via `rw` or `erw`, not `simp`. This shows the missing canonical simp lemma is a real, repeated cost.
findings.proposed_change: In Definitions/Def_CerednikDrinfeld_FormalUpperHalfPlaneDatum.lean, right after `inclBaseChange`, add `@[simp] theorem inclBaseChange_tmul {M' M : FullLattice 𝒪 K} (h : M'.1 ≤ M.1) (b : B) (v : ↥M'.1) : inclBaseChange B h (b ⊗ₜ[𝒪] v) = b ⊗ₜ[𝒪] (⟨v, h v.2⟩ : ↥M.1) := rfl`. The left side is a function applied to a tensor and the right side is a normal-form tensor, so this orientation cannot loop. Delete the duplicated per-file copies. Replace `hincl` and `rw [hincl] at hpush` here with `simp only [inclBaseChange_tmul] at hpush`, or `rw [inclBaseChange_tmul] at hpush`.
findings.benefit: Every proof that pushes a pure tensor through the lattice inclusion gets a single, canonical, simp-normalising rule. This removes the repeated private re-declarations and the ad hoc `rfl` have-statements. It also lets `simp` finish goals that mix `inclBaseChange` with `tmul` expressions.
